findings.title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false with inverted flag check and nil-unsafe dereference
findings.body: In pkg/expr/reader.go enableSqlExpressions does `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(FlagSqlExpressions)` then returns false in both branches, so it always returns false. The negation is backwards (true when the flag is off) and dead, so a future maintainer fixing it to `return true` will enable SQL when the flag is off and disable it when on. It also unconditionally dereferences h.features; previously QueryTypeSQL had no feature check, so any caller constructing ExpressionQueryReader with nil FeatureToggles will now panic on IsEnabledGlobally instead of getting a clean error. It should just return false with a comment, or nil-guard the toggles.

findings.title: Legacy SQL ingestion path has no explicit disable check
findings.body: pkg/expr/reader.go now explicitly rejects QueryTypeSQL in ReadQuery, but pkg/expr/sql_command.go UnmarshalSQLCommand/NewSQLCommand have no such gate. They are only incidentally blocked because pkg/expr/sql/db.go is a stub returning 'not implemented' from TablesList/QueryFramesInto. That leaves two entry points with different errors, no defense-in-depth, and silent re-enablement of the DuckDB RCE/LFI surface if the DB implementation is ever restored. Both constructors should explicitly return a disabled error consistent with ReadQuery.
